publicationStmt.p: Tag layer of the DHSS Meta-Tagging Project. The article text is reproduced from the staged copy named in sourceDesc and is not altered; the tags are held separately in standOff so that overlapping and nested spans are preserved.

bibl.title: Exploring the impact of artificial intelligence application in personalized learning environments: thematic analysis of undergraduates’ perceptions in China

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: existence
span.quote: The findings underscore the positive impact of generative AI on students’ motivation and cognitive skills, alongside concerns regarding potential overreliance leading to a decline in independent thinking.

span.label: undergraduates' perceptions of generative AI in personalized learning
span.quote: This paper delves into the perceptions and experiences of undergraduate students in Chinese universities concerning AI’s application in personalized learning.

span.label: observational-study
span.quote: The study surveyed 48 undergraduates from a comprehensive Chinese university who had utilized generative AI, gathering their insights through semi-structured interviews.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: AI supplies instant feedback and flags common mistakes, which triggers student self-reflection and thereby develops cognitive and thinking skills
span.quote: Thematic analysis revealed that AI tools are instrumental in providing instant feedback and highlighting common mistakes, which contribute to cognitive and thinking skill development (Theme 4).

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: the same personalization and tutoring that improves the learning experience invites excessive reliance, which erodes learner autonomy and critical thinking
span.quote: Although AI-generated personalized recommendations and intelligent tutoring systems significantly enhance online learning experiences, excessive reliance may undermine autonomy and critical thinking.

span.label: Small sample and purely qualitative data limit generalizability and may carry subjective bias.
span.note: what this limits: the generalisability of every finding: THE LIMITED SAMPLE SIZE ... AND THE EXCLUSIVE RELIANCE ON QUALITATIVE DATA
span.quote: The study acknowledges several limitations, including the limited sample size, which restricts the generalizability of the findings, and the exclusive reliance on qualitative data, which may introduce subjective biases.

span.label: No long-term or longitudinal evidence about sustained effects of AI use on learning, cognition or motivation.
span.note: what this limits: any claim about sustained effects: THE STUDY DOES NOT ADDRESS THE LONG-TERM EFFECTS OF AI USAGE IN EDUCATION
span.quote: Additionally, the study does not address the long-term effects of AI usage in education, emphasizing the need for longitudinal research to examine the sustained impact of AI on student learning outcomes, cognitive development, and motivation.

span.label: Three limits are stated together: a small sample, exclusive reliance on qualitative data with subjective bias, and no long-term effects.
span.note: what this limits: these findings as evidence about AI in personalised learning generally: the authors name a limited sample, exclusive reliance on qualitative data which may introduce subjective biases, and no treatment of long-term effects
span.quote: The study acknowledges several limitations, including the limited sample size, which restricts the generalizability of the findings, and the exclusive reliance on qualitative data, which may introduce subjective biases. Additionally, the study does not address the long-term effects of AI usage in education

span.label: The central construct is measured through instruments derived from a taxonomy, so the result inherits that taxonomy's division of cognition.
span.note: what this limits: a claim about cognitive skills in this study: they are measured with tools developed under guidance from Bloom's Taxonomy, which fixes which abilities count
span.quote: Cognitive skills, such as memory, attention, comprehension, and reasoning abilities, are measured through tools developed with guidance from Bloom’s Taxonomy.

span.label: The paper describes its own data collection two incompatible ways. Methods: interviews of about 30 minutes, audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim. Data availability: a survey of 10 questions answered as real-time feedback posted directly on a forum. These are different instruments producing different data, and the abstract uses both words in one sentence ('surveyed 48 undergraduates ... through semi-structured interviews'). Nothing in the paper reconciles them.
span.quote: Data collection was carried out through a survey of 10 questions distributed via the Personal Learning Environment (PLE) platform, where students provided real-time feedback directly on the forum.

span.label: The 90% agreement is computed after the two coders built the themes together: the preliminary codes were 'collaboratively discussed and categorized into potential themes by both the first and second authors', and only then did each researcher independently apply them. The figure measures consistency of application, not independent arrival at the same scheme.
span.quote: preliminary codes were then collaboratively discussed and categorized into potential themes by both the first and second authors. This collaborative phase was critical for maintaining a rigorous and unbiased coding process. Each researcher independently applied these codes

span.label: The sample is selected on the exposure under study - students who chose to enrol in an 'AI in Academic Writing' course - and the paper offers that selection as what makes the data informative rather than as a threat to it. Perceptions of AI are then reported from a group defined by having opted into using AI.
span.quote: Students were selected through convenience sampling, focusing on those who had chosen to enroll in the “AI in Academic Writing” course. This approach allowed us to gather insights from participants who were already interested and engaged in using AI tools as part of their academic development.

span.label: The paper recommends that future work 'employ quantitative methods alongside qualitative approaches to validate observed trends', while its own results are reported almost entirely as counts out of 48 - 35, 29, 25, 24, 22, 21, 18, 15, 10, 9 students and so on. The trends it asks future work to validate quantitatively are already stated as numbers here.
span.quote: Future research should consider larger and more diverse sample populations to enhance the generalizability of findings and employ quantitative methods alongside qualitative approaches to validate observed trends comprehensively.

span.label: A PROCEDURAL SAFEGUARD ON INSTRUMENT DESIGN: each interview question grounded in both a theoretical definition and actual student responses
span.note: eliminates: construct drift between what the instrument asks and what it claims to measure - a question written only from theory can miss how students actually talk, and one written only from their words can measure something the construct does not name
span.quote: To ensure that the instruments effectively capture the intended constructs, each question is grounded in both theoretical definitions and practical student responses.

span.label: cognitive skills
span.quote: Cognitive skills, such as memory, attention, comprehension, and reasoning abilities

span.label: personalized learning
span.quote: This paper delves into the perceptions and experiences of undergraduate students in Chinese universities concerning AI’s application in personalized learning.

span.label: generative AI
span.quote: there remains a notable gap in understanding how generative AI specifically facilitates the development of personalized learning experiences and cognitive skills in educational settings.

span.label: semi-structured interview
span.quote: The assessment tool used was a semi-structured interview structured around Bloom’s Taxonomy and Ryan and Deci’s Self- Determination Theory.

span.label: convenience sampling
span.quote: Students were selected through convenience sampling, focusing on those who had chosen to enroll in the “AI in Academic Writing” course. This approach allowed us to gather insights from participants who were already interested and engaged in using AI tools as part of their academic development.

span.label: thematic analysis
span.quote: Data analysis in this study was rigorously performed using thematic analysis, a method well-established for its effectiveness in qualitative research.

span.label: motivation
span.quote: For example, “Do you think generative AI can stimulate your learning motivation and interest? If so, how does generative AI stimulate your learning motivation and interest?”

span.label: cognitive skills - operationalised through Bloom's Taxonomy: memory, attention, comprehension and reasoning, as measured by tools built under that taxonomy's guidance
span.quote: Cognitive skills, such as memory, attention, comprehension, and reasoning abilities

span.label: AI assistance - AS EXPERIENCED BY A PARTICIPANT: a failure mode in which attempting to correct the system can INCREASE its misunderstanding rather than reduce it
span.quote: AI’s understanding of sentences cannot be satisfactory, and the correction process may even increase its misunderstanding.

span.label: the data - AS METHODS DESCRIBES IT: interviews of about 30 minutes, audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim by transcription software, then reviewed and edited
span.quote: The interviews were audio-recorded and transcribed verbatim using transcription software to maintain data integrity

span.label: the data - AS DATA AVAILABILITY DESCRIBES IT: a survey of 10 questions on a platform, answered as real-time feedback posted directly on a forum. NOT THE SAME INSTRUMENT as the transcribed 30-minute interviews of the methods section
span.quote: Data collection was carried out through a survey of 10 questions distributed via the Personal Learning Environment (PLE) platform, where students provided real-time feedback directly on the forum.

span.label: replicates → Mao, Chen, and Liu (2024)
span.quote: These findings are consistent with the observations of Mao, Chen, and Liu (2024), who noted that AI can spur creativity by providing diverse perspectives and innovative solutions.

span.label: replicates → Seo et al. (2021)
span.quote: This aligns with the work of Seo et al. (2021), who demonstrated that AI systems enhance online education through personalized support, automation of routine tasks, and adaptive assessments.

span.label: replicates → Ghimire et al. (2024)
span.quote: This variability in effectiveness aligns with observations by Ghimire et al. (2024), who highlighted that the performance of AI language models can be inconsistent depending on the complexity of the tasks.

span.label: builds-on → Vasconcelos et al. (2023); Passi and Vorvoreanu (2022)
span.quote: This concern is supported by Vasconcelos et al. (2023), who noted the tendency of individuals to accept AI-generated recommendations even when incorrect, and Passi and Vorvoreanu (2022), who discussed the challenges users face in evaluating their reliance on AI systems.

span.label: motivation —operationalised-as→ semi-structured interview
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE QUESTION CONTAINS THE ANSWER. 'Do you think generative AI can stimulate your learning motivation and interest? IF SO, HOW DOES generative AI stimulate your learning motivation and interest?' The yes/no is followed by a how-question that presupposes the yes, so a student who agrees is immediately asked to supply the mechanism. The reported result is the count of students who agreed.
span.quote: For example, “Do you think generative AI can stimulate your learning motivation and interest? If so, how does generative AI stimulate your learning motivation and interest?”

span.label: cognitive skills —operationalised-as→ semi-structured interview
span.note: strength of the relation: 0.9 — THE SAME SHAPE ON THE OTHER CONSTRUCT: 'Do you think generative AI can enhance your higher-order thinking ... IF SO, HOW DOES AI achieve the enhancement of these abilities?' Both of the paper's two constructs are elicited by a question whose second clause presupposes the effect. The construct is not measured; AGREEMENT WITH A PROPOSITION ABOUT THE CONSTRUCT IS. (This span is column-interleaved in the staged PDF text - 'the students' problemthese abilities?' - so the quote is exact but the paper's line order is not recoverable from it.)
span.quote: For cognitive skills, questions such as, “Do you think generative AI can enhance your higher-order thinking, and thinking abilities, problem-solving abilities? If so, how does AI achieve the students’ problemthese abilities?

span.label: inter-rater agreement
span.quote: The final stage of the analysis saw both researchers achieving an agreement of over 90% on the themes, codes, and quotations.

span.label: The most frequently reported benefit was that generative AI helped with homework and exam preparation by offering problem-solving strategies, refining articles and creating course content (35 of 48 students).
span.quote: For instance, 35 students reported that generative AI is particularly effective in assisting with homework and exam preparation by offering problem-solving strategies, refining articles, and creating course content.

span.label: Forty-two students said AI raised their enthusiasm by supplying learning resources and suggestions tailored to their own learning behaviour, interests and past performance.
span.quote: Specifically, 42 students noted that AI provides customized learning resources and interests, and suggestions tailored to their learning behavior, historical performance, making learning more targeted and effective.

span.label: Thirty-three students credited generative AI with fostering their creativity by supplying diverse perspectives and innovative solutions.
span.quote: 33 students noted that AI fosters creativity by offering diverse perspectives and innovative solutions.

span.label: The dominant student concern was that heavy reliance on AI would erode their ability to think independently (22 of 48 students).
span.quote: 22 students worry that excessive reliance on AI could diminish their ability to think independently.

span.label: Twenty-one students said AI-generated content was sometimes erroneous or inaccurate, so they had to verify and filter it themselves.
span.quote: 21 students reported that the content generated by AI tools could sometimes be erroneous or inaccurate, necessitating user verification and filtering.

span.label: Twenty-five students were worried about data security and privacy because of the volume of personal data AI systems process.
span.quote: 25 students expressed concerns about data security and privacy, especially given the large volumes of personal data that AI systems often handle.

span.label: Fifteen students said the AI tools failed to fully understand their queries and returned answers below their expectations.
span.quote: 15 students reported that AI tools sometimes failed to fully comprehend their queries, resulting in responses that fell short of their expectations.

span.label: personalized learning environment (PLE)
span.quote: A personalized learning environment, by definition, tailors the educational experience to meet individual learners’ specific needs and preferences.

span.label: personalized learning environments (PLEs) as adaptive systems
span.term: personalized learning environments (PLEs) as adaptive systems
span.quote: Personalized learning environments (PLEs) are designed to cater to students’ interests, needs, readiness, and motivation, making adaptive adjustments based on their progress to support lifelong learning.

span.label: engagement
span.quote: Engagement describes the level of active participation and involvement in educational activities, reflected in students’ interactions, feedback, and interest in the learning process.

span.label: motivation
span.quote: Motivation includes both intrinsic factors, such as curiosity and personal satisfaction, and extrinsic factors, like grades and rewards, that drive students to engage in learning activities.

span.label: required use of generative AI within the course
span.term: required use of generative AI within the course
span.quote: The course, worth 2 credits, was chosen for this study because it directly integrates AI into the curriculum, requiring students to engage with a designated AI platform for at least four hours weekly.

span.label: cognitive skills (memory, attention, comprehension, reasoning)
span.quote: Cognitive skills, such as memory, attention, comprehension, and reasoning abilities, are measured through tools developed with guidance from Bloom’s Taxonomy.

span.label: motivation (intrinsic and extrinsic)
span.quote: Motivation is explored through Ryan and Deci’s Self-Determination Theory, which helps us evaluate both intrinsic factors, like personal satisfaction and curiosity, and extrinsic factors, rewards and recognition, to determine how AI tools affect these motivational drivers.

span.label: learning engagement
span.quote: Engagement is evaluated through questions that ask about the frequency and depth of AI tool usage, such as, “How do you think generative AI can enhance your learning engagement on online learning platforms (such as Personal Learning Environment PLE platforms)?”

span.label: 48 — number of undergraduate interviewees in the study
span.quote: The study surveyed 48 undergraduates from a comprehensive Chinese university who had utilized generative AI, gathering their insights through semi-structured interviews.

span.label: 23 males and 25 females, aged between 18 and 21 — sex and age composition of the student cohort
span.quote: The cohort includes 23 males and 25 females, aged between 18 and 21.

span.label: over 90% — agreement between the two coders on themes, codes and quotations
span.quote: The final stage of the analysis saw both researchers achieving an agreement of over 90% on the themes, codes, and quotations.

span.label: four hours weekly — minimum required AI-platform use per student per week
span.quote: Each student has committed to using a designated AI platform for a minimum of four hours weekly.

span.label: 35 — students reporting AI helped with homework and exam preparation
span.quote: For instance, 35 students reported that generative AI is particularly effective in assisting with homework and exam preparation by offering problem-solving strategies, refining articles, and creating course content.

span.label: 42 — students reporting AI-customized resources boosted their enthusiasm
span.quote: Specifically, 42 students noted that AI provides customized learning resources and interests, and suggestions tailored to their learning behavior, historical performance, making learning more targeted and effective.

span.label: 22 — students fearing over-reliance would reduce independent thinking
span.quote: 22 students worry that excessive reliance on AI could diminish their ability to think independently.

p.note: The full text of this article is not redistributable, so it is not included here. Every tag above carries the exact sentence it was made from, quoted under fair quotation. The article itself is at https://doi.org/10.1057/s41599-024-04168-x.
